result.markdown: --- title: "R-Guide" author: "Pawan" date: "2026-05-10" output: html_document --- [](https://www.r-project.org/about.html) # Getting Started with R R is one of the most popular programming languages in statistical computing. It’s an open-source, easy to learn, and easy to use for manipulating statistical data. This R guide will cover a basic overview of getting started with R. # Download and Install R and Rstudio [Rstudio](https://www.rstudio.com/products/rstudio/download/) [R](https://cran.r-project.org/) ## Installing R and RStudio on Linux Install the R-base package using the following code or Use your package manager to install R and R-studio. ### Debian/Ubuntu/Linux Mint `apt-get install r-base` (as superuser) or `sudo apt-get install r-base` ### Install RStudio on Linux To install RStudio, go to download RStudio, click on the download button for RStudio desktop, click the link for the latest RStudio version. Download the correct version of R-Studio from https://www.rstudio.com/products/rstudio/download/#download `sudo apt install -f ./file-path` (e.g. ~/Downloads/rstudio-2022.12.0-353-amd64.deb) Other way to install RStudio use the following command `sudo apt-get install rstudio-desktop` ## Installing R and RStudio on Window To install R and RStudio on Window, go through the following steps: ### Install R on windows Step – 1: Go to R project website. Step – 2: Click on the Download R for Windows link and save the .exe file. Step – 3: Run the .exe file and follow the installation instructions. ### Install RStudio on Windows Step – 1: Go to download RStudio and click on the download button for RStudio desktop. Step – 2: Click on the link for the windows version of RStudio and save the .exe file. Step – 3: Run the .exe and follow the installation instructions. ## Installing R and RStudio on Mac OS To install R and RStudio on Mac OS, go through the following steps: ### Install R on Mac Step – 1: Go to CRAN R Project Website. Step – 2: Click on the Download for Mac OS link. Step – 3: Click on the link for the pkg file of the latest R version and save it. Step – 4: Double click the downloaded file and follow installation instructions. ### Install RStudio on Mac OS Step – 1: Go to download RStudio and click on the download button for the RStudio desktop. Step – 2: Click on the link for the Mac OS RStudio and save the .dmg file. Step – 3: Double click the downloaded file and then drag-and-drop it into your applications folder. Note:- Download suitable version of R and RStudio according to Mac OS version # The Working Directory The working directory is a file path that R will use as the starting point for relative file paths. That is, it's the default location for importing and exporting files. An example of a working directory looks like "/file/path" ``` #Returns your current working directory getwd() #Changes your current working directory to a desired file path setwd("~/R") ``` # Using Packages in R R packages are collections of functions and tools developed by the R community. They increase the power of R by improving existing base R functionalities, or by adding new ones. ``` # Lets you install new packages (e.g., tidyverse package) install.packages("tidyverse") #Lets you load and use packages (e.g., tidyverse package) library(tidyverse) ``` # Vector in R Vector is one-dimension arrays that can hold numeric data, character data, or logical data. In other words, a vector is a simple tool to store data. ## Types of Vector 1. Numeric Vector (e.g 1,2,3) - Numeric vector can be a numeric or an integer. 2. Characters (e.g "a", "b", "r-language",) 3. Factor (categorize the data and store it as levels) 4. Boolean (True/False) ## Creating Vectors in R - There are two ways to create a vector i) using comma (,), ii) using colon (:) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ## Numeric Vector c(1,3,5) ## numeric c(1:7) ## integer ## Character Vector c("a","b","hello") ``` ::: Here "c" means "combine", and which is represent as the vector is an one dimensional. - We can store or save vector using this "->" ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} c(1:10)->v v c(1,2,3,4)->v1 v1 c("my","vector")->vector vector ``` ::: - Check vector ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} class(v) class(v1) class(vector) ``` ::: - Create a vector with a specified interval between each element ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} seq(1,20,by = 3) ## Same as c(seq(1,20,by = 3)) ``` ::: - We can create a vector of with repeated elements as well a number of times ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rep(3, times = 4) rep(3,4) rep(c(1:4), times = 4) rep(c(1:4),each = 4) ``` ::: ## Vector Functions in R + `sort(my_vector)` : Returns my_vector sorted + `rev(my_vector)` : Reverses the order of my_vector + `table(my_vector)` : Count the values in a vector + `unique(my_vector)` : Distinct elements in a vector ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ## First let's create a dummy vecrtor c(1,3,5,2,7,4,9,24,12,25,13,22,12,3,4,6,10,9,25,22,22,21,12)->a a sort(a) rev(a) table(a) unique(a) ``` ::: # Data Frames A data frame has a data set of columns and rows. The basic syntex of data frame we can write as DF(row, column) or we can also write as DF[i,j] Here, i refer to row and j refer to column. Note that the first argument before comma always specify the row and the second argument after the comma specify the column e.g. ```data[1:9,c(2,5,6)]``` the first nine rows and column no 2, 5 and 6. Basically, a data frame is a set collection of vectors. In a data frame every column represent a particular type of vector (numeric, character, factor). + Let's creates the data frame named as df ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data.frame(x = 1:7, y = c("Sun","Mon","Tue","Wed","Thurs","Fri","Sat")) -> df df ``` ::: Using as.data.frame command we can change a vector to data frame. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df[ ,2] ##selects all columns of the second row ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df$x ## selects the column x ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df[2, ] ## selects all rows of the second column ``` ::: # Combine two Data Frames We can combine two data frames by coloumns or by rows as well ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df1 <- data.frame(x = 1:3, y = c("a", "b", "c"), z = 12:14) df2 <- data.frame(x = 4:6, y = c("A", "B", "C"), z = 21:23) cbind(df1,df2) ## by coloumns rbind(df1,df2) ## by rows ``` ::: ## Subset of Data frame We can also pick a subset from data frame ```subset(data1,var1>10000)->data2``` A subset of data frame data1 and store it into data2, which will be also a data frame. ```subset(data1,select=c("var1","var5","var10"))->data2 ``` Also we can select a subset by selecting particular columns as we want. ## Data Table in R
